creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 5. Declaring `<variadic positionals> -flag v1 v2` isn't possible, and attempting it fills a positional with no error.

With `first str` / `second str = ""` / `filter c str[] = []`:

```
mycmd tok -c c1 c2
// first=tok  second=c2  filter=["c1"]     no error
```

A list flag consumes exactly one value, so `c2` falls through to the next free positional. Two variadics type-check but the second is always `[]`, and usage prints no positional forms. #153's own reading: "The documented left-to-right rule is doing exactly what it says, which is why nothing fires."

This is the other half of #148.1. That item is the variadic stopping at a flag; this is the flag not resuming after itself. **Greedy bare-value collection for list flags closes both.** Fix lives in `ra`.

The workaround is its own finding: don't declare the flag at all, and let `-c` reach `*token` as plain data. `-h` and globals still work, but a typo'd flag silently becomes data, so the script hand-rolls the `-`-prefix rejection a declared flag would have given free.

Demand signal from the same issue: three sibling scripts now carry the same copy-pasted NOTE paragraph in their `--help` explaining flag placement.

---

### Orientation

- The card is right that the fix lives in `ra`, not in this repo. `github.com/amterp/ra` is first-party - AGENTS.md treats the `amterp/` deps as extensions of this codebase, and a workaround in Rad would be debt filed in the wrong repo. Checkout at `~/src/ra`; `go.mod` pins `v0.8.1`.
- `core/args.go` is Rad's side of the boundary: it translates declared script args into `ra` flags. `core/args.go:339-340` and `core/args.go:558-559` are where `SetVariadic(true)` gets applied when the script arg is variadic.
- Iterate with a local `replace github.com/amterp/ra => /Users/amterp/src/ra` in `go.mod`, and remove it before committing. `./dev --release` refuses to release with one present. Tagging and releasing `ra` stays with the user.

### Watch out for

- Greedy collection changes how existing argv parses. A script relying on `-c one two` leaving `two` for a positional silently changes behavior. Decide whether that needs a `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.X.md` entry and a `feat!:` / `fix!:` prefix.
- The variadic loop's `wouldParseAsFlag` check (`ra_cmd_parse.go:1552`) exists because an earlier version parsed candidate tokens to probe them, which executed every later flag in the argv once per probe and duplicated slice values. Any new collection logic must stay side-effect free the same way.
- `ra_completion.go:421-431` and `ra_completion.go:536` `isVariadicFlag` encode assumptions about how many positions a variadic absorbs. They have to agree with whatever collection rule lands, or completion drifts from parsing.
- Rad's own embedded commands (`core/embedded/`) are Rad scripts parsed through the same `ra` path, so an argv-parsing change can break `rad new`, `rad check`, `rad fmt` and friends. `make all` covers them.
title: Fix the silent misparse when a list flag follows variadic positionals
